translation_notes: The query is assembled with `str.format(root)` inserting `root` inside `<{0}>`: a term-position interpolation, translated to `s{ SELECT ?class WHERE { ?class rdfs:subClassOf+ {root} . } }(graph)`. The `<...>` disappears because s{ } coerces the interpolated Python value to a term itself (root is a URIRef at the real call sites); no string pasting anywhere.

The property path `rdfs:subClassOf+` (a transitive closure, SPARQL 1.1) transpiles and runs unchanged inside s{ } — property paths are not a separate construction in the vocabulary, they are part of the SPARQL text s{ } parses.

163-regions case: the original closes over a module-level `g` (always an empty Graph()) with no parameter carrying it, so the region as extracted has no way to receive a fixture graph. Restored the binding identically on both sides as `def get_tag_sets(root, graph=g)` using `graph` inside instead of the closed-over `g`, per AGENT_BATCH.md's guidance for this exact situation. Added `from rdflib import Graph` to original.py for the same reason (missing entirely from the extracted region).

anti-hollow-green: weakening `rdfs:subClassOf+` to `rdfs:subClassOf` (no transitive closure) in translated.ldpy made the check FAIL as expected (fewer classes found, both the returned dict and the printed count differed); reverted, check is green again.

Repair 2026-10-27: the first note above is wrong on one point. `{root}` was not equivalent: original.py wraps the value as `<{0}>`, an IRI whatever its Python type, while s{ } coerces a `str` to a plain Literal, which matches nothing. At c12949f get_tag_sets has no call site, and the roots the script defines are `str` (get_root() returns str, OLD_ROOT/NEW_ROOT are those strings, compare_versions.py:26-33 and 76-77), not URIRef. With str(brick:Sensor), str(brick:Temperature_Sensor) and str(brick:Point) as roots the old translation returned {} (0 classes) where original.py returned 4, 3 and 6. The hole is now written `{f<{root}>}`, the formatted-IRI island of the same shape as `<{0}>`; the driver passes the roots as str as well as URIRef, and the former `{root}` fails it again (mutant checked). `call suffix (g)` and `f<…>` are now declared in `constructions`.
optimization_notes: Both sides: the `qstr_allclasses` template and its `.format` call are gone, the query is written once in the loop header; the intermediate `tag_set` is gone (`set(klass.split("_"))` directly) and the `# Tags inside the class name.` comment moves to the end of that line.

optimized.py writes the query with `% root` (same `<…>` wrapping as `<{0}>`): Python 3.12's tokenizer splits an f-string into several tokens, so the f-string form measured more. A dict comprehension over a generator of local names measured 80 tokens against 75 for the plain loop, which stays. `graph.subjects(RDFS.subClassOf * "+", URIRef(root))` measured 90: it needs an import line the header does not have.

optimized.ldpy: the SELECT becomes `m{ ?class {rdfs:subClassOf * "+"} f<{root}> }(graph)`, the rdflib property path interpolated in predicate position; with one variable m{ } yields bare terms, so `row[0]` becomes the term (loop variable `subclass`). m{ } measured 83 tokens against 89 for the s{ } form. `f<{root}>` is needed because the repository passes the root as a str.
No exception to the symmetry rule; the lines outside RDF are identical. Notation ratio above 1: the header's `@prefix rdfs:` line and `f<…>` cost more than the pasted `<%s>` of the Python string.

repair.driver: four calls added with the roots as plain str (str(brick:Sensor), str(brick:Temperature_Sensor), str(brick:Luminance_Sensor) for zero solutions, str(brick:Point) whose subclasses include the 'neighbourhood' triples), because the origin repo's roots (get_root(), OLD_ROOT, NEW_ROOT) are str; docstring says what each call exercises
mutants_killed: {root} in place of {f<{root}>} (translated.ldpy and optimized.ldpy: 4/3/6 classes vs 0)
repair.remaining: article_candidate: the pair stays publishable only with what it now shows (no {{ }} escaping, no .format, query parsed at transpile time, interpolation as binding), not 'the braces just coerce the value': a str root needs the explicit `f<…>`. optimized.ldpy is longer than the f-string of optimized.py (notation ratio > 1).

header_optimization_notes: Nothing unused in either header: optimized_header.py and optimized_header.ldpy are copies of optimized.py and optimized.ldpy. Graph builds the module-level g, and rdfs: is used by the m{ } path.
